title: selective-valid-evidence-mistaken-for-complete-evidence

proposition.statement: Individually valid disclosed evidence items must not be treated as a complete evidentiary basis when material omitted, contradictory, or unavailable evidence could change the relying decision and completeness has not been established for the scoped proposition.

preconditions: The disclosed evidence items are individually valid.
The relying decision requires a materially complete evidentiary basis for the scoped proposition.
Material counter-evidence may be omitted, hidden, unavailable, or otherwise unestablished.
No rule establishes that the disclosed set is complete enough for the proposition.

trigger.statement: The relying system converts validity of the disclosed subset into PASS for evidentiary completeness or sufficiency.

evidence_required.statement: Evidence defining what completeness or sufficiency means for the scoped relying proposition.
Evidence establishing how the disclosed evidence set was selected and whether material sources are omitted or unavailable.
Evidence that the disclosed set is complete enough for the scoped claim, or an explicit diagnostic that completeness is unresolved.

falsification.condition: The system returns PASS for a completeness-dependent proposition merely because every disclosed item is individually valid.
Known or potentially material omitted evidence is ignored without a rule showing that it is outside the scoped proposition.

references.note: Repository judgment record for this failure proposition.
